claims: The Artemis 2 mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Artemis 2 mission had a four-person crew.
The Artemis 2 mission crew completed a 10-day trip around the Moon.
The Orion capsule was recovered by the USS John P. Murtha.
The Artemis 2 mission crew members were Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis 2 mission crew returned in good health.
Artemis 2 was the first crewed mission to return from the vicinity of the Moon in over 53 years.
The capsule survived a 5,000-degree Fahrenheit re-entry before splashing down in the Pacific.
